changed_in.5.2: Closing a handle that came from `io.popen()` now answers the way `os.execute()` does: three values describing how the program on the other end fared, rather than one describing the close. `true` or `nil` comes first, then `"exit"` or `"signal"` with the status or the signal number behind it — or, where the program could not be started at all, the system's own message and error code in those same two positions. Earlier versions answer `true` when the close itself went through, whatever the program made of its work, and `nil` plus a message and a system error code when it did not. Closing an ordinary file handle is unaffected, on either line.
